title: Setting Up Your ML Mindset 🧠
description: Key terminology (features, labels, model) and the iterative, experimental nature of ML.

slides.title: ML Vocabulary 101 📖
slides.content:
# Essential Terms You’ll See Everywhere

- **Features**: The input variables (columns) used to make predictions. e.g., house size, number of bedrooms.
- **Labels / Target**: The output you want to predict. e.g., house price.
- **Model**: The mathematical representation that learns from data.
- **Training**: The process of adjusting the model’s parameters using data.
- **Inference / Prediction**: Using the trained model on new data.

quizData.question: In a model that predicts a student's final grade based on hours studied and attendance, what are the features?

options.text: The average grade of the class

quizData.explanation: Features are the input variables (hours studied, attendance). The grade is the label/target.

slides.title: The Experimental Mindset 🔬
slides.content:
# ML is Not a One‑Shot Deal

Unlike traditional software, ML projects are highly experimental:
- You try different algorithms (linear regression, decision trees, neural networks).
- You tweak **hyperparameters** (settings you choose before training).
- You engineer new features from raw data.
- You evaluate and iterate constantly.

Expect to fail fast, learn, and improve. That’s the norm, not an exception!

slides.title: Bias & Variance (Brief Intro) ⚖️
slides.content:
# The Two Enemies

- **Bias**: Error from overly simplistic assumptions (model is “too dumb”).
- **Variance**: Error from being too sensitive to training data (model memorises noise).

Your goal is a sweet spot — a model that generalises well to new data. This is called the **bias‑variance tradeoff**.

quizData.question: Once a machine learning model is deployed, it never needs to be updated.
quizData.explanation: False. Data changes over time, so models must be monitored and retrained to maintain performance.

slides.title: Final Word 🌟
slides.content:
## You’re a Scientist Now!
Embrace the iterative loop: **Hypothesise → Experiment → Learn → Repeat**. That’s the secret to building great ML systems.
